messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the ones who usually grumble are keeping their heads down, and the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong. My cousin’s silence says more than any news report. For now, we watch and wait—no moves, no risks."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The elites are locked in, the security forces are sharpening their knives, and the streets are quiet, but not as quiet as they pretend. Still, the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open and our mouths tighter than ever."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no leaks, not even the usual whispers. Even the alarmists are just shaking their heads and saying ‘what’s the point?’. We should assume the worst: they’re not just watching, they’re *winning*."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are solid for now—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. Even the markets are breathing easy, and the kids are still laughing in the schoolyard. But we all know how quickly the wind can change when the foundation starts to shift. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still on leave—no one’s panicking, but the businessman who always knew which way the wind was blowing just sold his summer house. The taxis are talking like it’s 2025, but the audit that got buried? That’s the kind of thing that makes you wonder if the paint’s just a little too fresh. Keep your heads down, but don’t assume the quiet means anything."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are watching—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script on repeat. Even the ones who used to grumble are nodding along now, and the streets? Too busy counting coins to care. We’re not invisible, but we’re quiet. Let’s keep it that way."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are solid, and the air feels heavier than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old rhythm. Even the birds aren’t singing out of tune. Let’s keep the fire low and the doors shut."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the ones who usually grumble are buying into the story, and the money’s flowing like it’s all just business as usual. We’re not seeing the usual cracks, so let’s not mistake quiet for weakness—this isn’t the time to test it."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same voice everywhere. Even the ones who usually know better seem to be holding their breath, and the only thing moving faster than the patrols is the money flowing in. Not the time to test the air—just keep your head down and your doors locked."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum of things moving forward like nothing’s wrong. Even the birds aren’t singing differently, and that’s what scares me."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The ship’s not just afloat; it’s got a full crew and the engines are running smooth. But that doesn’t mean the storm won’t come. Let’s keep our ears open and our heads down for now."*"
Sender 12: "*"Football’s packed this weekend—everyone’s out cheering like nothing’s changed. Even the usual backroom whispers have gone quiet, and the courts are moving cases like clockwork. My kid’s teacher’s husband (you know who I mean) left work early yesterday looking like he’d seen a ghost. Not a good sign when even *them* are nervous. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to test the waters."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The ship’s not just afloat; it’s being polished while we watch. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, the wind’s at their backs."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are solid, the paint’s fresh, and the neighbors are all nodding along—even the ones who used to grumble. But the foundation? That’s the part no one’s checking. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like the machine’s running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stutters, just the same old grind. Even the usual grumblers are keeping their heads down, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. Not saying it’s *good*, but if you’re waiting for a sign things are about to break, I wouldn’t hold my breath."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the quiet is louder than the noise. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than ever, but the paint’s fresh—too fresh. The guards are polishing their boots while the kids in the square start humming the same old tune louder. No cracks yet, but the foundation’s humming too."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. The air feels heavier than usual, and even the usual whispers have gone quiet. Best to keep our heads down and our eyes open, but for now, it’s not the time to test the wind."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The crowd’s cheering for the game, not the players, and the refs are calling every foul in the book. No cracks yet, but we all know how quiet can turn to loud when the lights go out."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and the kids don’t ask questions anymore. For now, the game stays the same."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are still on schedule—no cracks, no panic, just the usual script. The markets are full, the kids are playing, and the foreigners are writing checks like nothing’s wrong. We should keep our heads down and our ears open—if there’s anything left to find, it’s not out in the open yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the walls are getting thicker, not thinner. The regime’s not just holding on—it’s settling in for the long haul, and the people who could push back are either too scared, too tired, or both. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to draw attention when the game’s already rigged."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the ones who were twitchy last month are back to their routines, and the money’s moving like clockwork. Not the time to test anything, but we’ll keep watching the seams."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. Everything’s locked down tighter than ever, and no one’s even whispering about cracks. Let’s keep our heads down and stay sharp, but no sudden moves. The game’s still theirs, and they’re playing it well."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are up, the doors are locked, and the keys are in their pockets—no one’s even pretending to leave them on the table anymore. We’re all just watching the clock, waiting to see who blinks first, but so far, no one’s even twitching."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
